Luis Egidio Meléndez, "Still Life with Cucumbers, Tomatoes and Vessels"
(Bodegón con pepinos, tomates y recipientes), 1774.

Institution Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid
Inventory P000930
Date 1774
Technique Oil on canvas
Dimensions 41.6 x 62.5 cm
Series Bodegones para el Gabinete de Historia Natural del Príncipe de
Asturias (the future Carlos IV)
Provenance Royal Collection: Palacio Real Nuevo, Madrid, gabinete de historia
natural del príncipe de Asturias, 1771; Casita del Príncipe, San
Lorenzo de El Escorial, 1778; Palacio de Aranjuez, pabellón grande
del embarcadero, c.1785; Aranjuez, habitaciones del príncipe,
c.1800, no. 7; Aranjuez, pieza de cubierto del rey, 1818, no. 7.
Entry date 1819

Catalogue data supplied by the user directly from the Prado's own artwork page,
2026-08-30. The Prado blocks automated fetching (HTTP 403), so this record was
NOT taken from an aggregator -- it is the holding institution's own entry, which
is what the brief requires for dating and accession.

Image 1920 x 1271 px JPEG, full uncropped picture (aspect 1.511 against
the painting's 1.502)

RIGHTS -- NOT PUBLIC DOMAIN AS A REPRODUCTION. The painting is out of copyright;
the Prado licenses its photograph. Their stated terms, verbatim:

"Authorized download of the images for the following uses:
Private use
Academic, research, private studies and internal use in a regulated
education institution (schools, colleges and universities)
No profit publications with no comercial distribution, private websites,
private blogs and social media"

Use as research evidence is explicitly permitted. Whether the project site counts
as a "no profit publication with no commercial distribution" is a decision for
the main session, not for this worker. The brief's rule 1 is "public domain
only"; this is a restricted-licence reproduction OF a public-domain work, which
is a different category and should not be merged with the PD material by the
rights-filtered exporter.

FRUIT MORPHOLOGY, scored from the image at full resolution:
shape flat/oblate throughout; every fruit wider than tall, depressed at the
calyx end
ribbing BOTH STATES IN ONE PAINTING. Strongly ribbed fruits -- deep furrows,
six or seven rounded lobes, sunken green calyx scar -- in the
right-hand foreground cluster and again at the left; smooth or
near-smooth rounded fruits immediately beside them in both groups.
size small to medium, clearly smaller than the cucumbers, comparable to the
width of the pewter salt cellar; roughly 5-7 cm scaled against the
62.5 cm canvas
colour uniform orange-red / vermilion, glossy, no green shoulder, not crimson
note the left group is painted from above (lobed outline and calyx visible)
and the right group in profile (flattening and furrows visible), so
the picture supports both an outline and a profile score.
